- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. This run read `content/docs` from `e0e4ea2620f8d47c0fd1d9d9b1135c5d6029b228` — the merge of head `623a8ecc5132e7fed870018922fcc5580599f900` into base `1708115e2f7c6e8cff913d954ed2b5ff7e80e2b2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e0e4ea2620f8d47c0fd1d9d9b1135c5d6029b228 && git checkout e0e4ea2620f8d47c0fd1d9d9b1135c5d6029b228
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1708115e2f7c6e8cff913d954ed2b5ff7e80e2b2 623a8ecc5132e7fed870018922fcc5580599f900 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1708115e2f7c6e8cff913d954ed2b5ff7e80e2b2 && git merge --no-ff 623a8ecc5132e7fed870018922fcc5580599f900

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1708115e2f7c6e8cff913d954ed2b5ff7e80e2b2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set change the diff makes (right).** One narrowing of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s object save/publish/restore doors: an `object` whose `datasource` is a non-empty string other than `'default'` that resolves to nothing is refused `422 INVALID_METADATA`, one finding at `datasource`. Served over REST by `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/:name` (draft and live), `POST /api/v1/meta/object/:name/publish`, `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/publish-drafts`, and the rollback/revert doors. Nothing is widened. No public export changes: `unknownDatasourceSaveRefusal` is a `private` method on the class, the module function in `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts` is not re-exported by `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` (that index exports only `SDUI_MANIFEST_SERVICE` and the protocol class surface), `AuthoringGateHost`/`SaveDoorRefusalHost` are internal host shapes, and `promoteDraftForPublish`'s new `batchDatasources` is a parameter of a private method. `packages/qa/dogfood` is `private: true`, so it owes no changeset entry. Right.

**Seat question 1 — every door that now refuses, every door that still accepts.**
Doors that store an `object` and now refuse, read at the head:
- `saveMetaItem` draft mode and publish (live) mode, including `force`: the new block at `protocol.ts` sits after the schema gate and `externalBindingSaveRefusal`, before the authoring gate and `repo.put`. Every `PUT /meta/object/:name` and the runtime's own `meta` domain save (`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:1590`), the `_unpublished` app re-save in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:1917`, the organization-ownership ceremony (`organization-ownership.ts:903`) and `os migrate meta --stored` (`migrateStoredMetadata` re-saves rows through `saveMetaItem`) all route through it.
- `promoteDraftForPublish`, on the draft body before `repo.promoteDraft`: shared by `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts` (which passes `batchDatasources`, the batch's datasource draft names, computed from `drafts` with `canonicalMetaType(d.type) === 'datasource'`). A refusal inside the batch throws before the write, so the batch aborts like the other per-item refusals; the dogfood and protocol tests pin `outcome: 'refused'`, `published: []`.
- `rollbackMetaItem` and `revertCommit`, through `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses` (the host gained the member; the family test adds a `pinBothDoors` case). Right.
Doors read that do NOT store an object body and so are not in play: `installPackage`/`updatePackage` (`protocol-package-install.ts` writes `sys_packages` and the registry only); seeds (`seedApplied` is row data); flows (`automation.ts:1942` saves `FLOW_METADATA_TYPE`); permission-set clone (not an object). The code layer (`*.object.ts` loaded at boot by `registerApp`) is not a save door and is not judged by this diff; an unknown `datasource` declared in code stays a boot-time matter. No archive/zip install path stores object rows outside `saveMetaItem` (none found in `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`; `protocolSvc.installPackage` at 1492 takes a manifest only).
Doors that still accept it, by design and stated in the code: (a) an engine with no `getDriverByName` member refuses nothing (`IDataEngine.getDriverByName?` is optional in `packages/spec/src/contracts/data-engine.ts:358`; the real ObjectQL implements it as `this.drivers.get(name)`); (b) a write that keeps the binding the object already holds (question 2). Direct `sys_metadata` writes exist only inside `sys-metadata-repository.ts` (the bundle parent row), reached through `repo.put`. Verdict: no path that stores an object body is left lenient beyond those two declared exemptions. Right.

**Seat question 2 — what counts as known, and the held-binding exemption.** Read in `unknownDatasourceSaveRefusal`, in order:
- absent, `''` or `'default'`: pass (matches `resolveDatasourceBinding` step 1, which treats `'default'` as fall-through). Right.
- `engine.getDriverByName(name)` truthy: pass. Covers a `driver.*` service (ObjectQL `plugin.ts:1146` registers each into `drivers`), an `onEnable` `drivers.register`, and every declared datasource whose driver connected. Right.
- `readMetaItem({ type: 'datasource', name })` answers an item: pass. That read is environment-wide, active state only, no organization row, stored row first then the code layer's registry item; `AppPlugin.start()` registers every `*.datasource.ts` (and the config's `datasources` collection) in the metadata registry in memory as `origin: 'code'`, so a declared datasource whose driver failed or was evicted still resolves. "Same package" is therefore covered by the registry, and "declared in any package or stored in this environment" too. Right.
- pending: on a DRAFT save, any datasource draft of that name in the environment (`listDrafts({ type: 'datasource' })`, which excludes disabled packages' drafts and is not package-scoped); on `publishPackageDrafts`, only the batch's own datasource drafts; on `publishMetaItem`, on a LIVE save and on a restore, no draft counts. So a draft may name a draft, but nothing goes active naming one. The order-independence inside a batch is asserted by the test (object promoted before the datasource). Right.
- "registered by runtime config or a plugin that may start later": every HTTP save runs after `ObjectKernel.bootstrap()` has run every `init`/`start`/`onEnable`, so a plugin that registers in `onEnable` is visible by request time; a plugin not installed yet is unknown now, and refused — that is the card's ask. Right.
- The held-binding exemption: `current = readMetaItem({ type: 'object', name })` (the active stored row, else the code layer's definition, by name, environment-wide) and `current.datasource === datasource` passes. Exactly what it lets through: a draft save, live save, publish or restore of an object that ALREADY has an active definition carrying this same `datasource` string. A NEW object has no `current`, so it cannot be saved with a typo through this exemption; a typo under a different name than the active row holds is refused (the test's `gapdata_typo` leg). Residue it preserves: a pre-rule active row with a dangling binding keeps re-saving unchanged (the dev states this in Acceptance notes). A pre-rule DRAFT with a dangling binding and no active row is not exempt: its re-save and its publish are both refused, which is the strict side. One marginal note, not a flag: the read is keyed by object name, not by (name, package), so a save of the same object name into another package carrying the row's own dangling binding passes too; it names no datasource the active row does not already name, so it opens no new typo. Verdict on the dev's sentence "a held binding is not judged, which keeps os migrate re-saves working": accurate; `migrateStoredMetadata` and the ownership ceremony re-save stored bodies through `saveMetaItem` with the binding unchanged, and a declaration boot never runs `onEnable`, so without the exemption those re-saves would be refused for a driver registered there. Right.

**Seat question 4 — the engine-double ledger.** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains three rows for `protocol.unknown-datasource-refusal.test.ts` (`delete`, `findOne`, `update`, each `pinned: 1`); 15 additions, 0 deletions, no existing row changed. The new test's double calls `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`, `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` and `assertEngineFindOnePredicate`, which is what the rows pin. The restore-family stub adds only `getDriverByName`, not a write verb. An addition the new tests require; no pin loosened. Right. `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (where `check:engine-double-contract` runs) is success on the head.

**Seat question 5 — the envelope.** `err.code = 'INVALID_METADATA'`, `err.status = 422`, `err.issues = [{ path: 'datasource', code: 'custom', message }]`, `err.message` = `object/NAME failed spec validation: ${specValidationFindings(writeFace, issues)}` — byte-for-byte the construction `externalBindingSaveRefusal` uses at lines 299-302 of the same file. No new error code. The finding's message names both the object and the datasource ("Object 'NAME' names datasource 'DS', and no datasource of that name exists here: …") and the three remedies; the dogfood test pins `"path":"datasource"` and the sentence on the wire. Right.

**Seat question 6 — the dogfood battery.** The report (PR body and os-dev-report) says: on `79ec0859` the full battery exited 1, `Test Files 1 failed | 327 passed | 3 skipped (331)`, `Tests 2 failed | 2686 passed | 20 skipped (2708)`, both failures in `packaged-action-disabled-dispatch-live.dogfood.test.ts` (`acceptance[0]` read `after.done` true at line 153; `acceptance[5]`/`[2]` read a different action row id at line 244); that file passed alone on the same head twice (8/8, exit 0); the battery on `1735274f` (the same product tree; `79ec0859` adds a test double and a ledger row) exited 0 with 328 files passed. Not run here. Read at the head, that file boots its own showcase and exercises `sys_metadata_activation`, action dispatch over REST and MCP, and a cold reboot; it contains no `meta/object` save, no `datasource`, no `publish-drafts` and no call into the save doors this diff changes, and this diff adds behaviour only to the `object` save/publish/restore doors. It touches nothing this diff changes; the dev's reading (load-dependent flake, #26572's file, reported not skipped) is consistent with what the file does. Recorded; not a finding against this head. The CI dogfood shards were path-filtered off this head, so no second measure exists.

**Other derived judgments.**
- Placement in `saveMetaItem`: `mode === 'draft' ? 'drafts' : undefined` passes the draft set only in draft mode; a live save naming a draft-only datasource is refused. Right (the live object would route to no driver).
- In `promoteDraftForPublish` the refusal is asked only `if (draftForGate)`, on the draft body, beside the external-binding refusal that already uses that guard. Right.
- The restore doors ask with no `pending` and no `writeFace`: a restore writes an ACTIVE row. Right.
- The authoring-gate host `Pick` is widened to include the new member at the single call site in `protocol.ts:7057`. Right.
- Test-double limit the dev states (the protocol double's `transaction` does not roll back the sibling) is honest and the dogfood control over the real stack covers the batch path. Right.
- PR title `fix(metadata-protocol)!:`, BREAKING banner and the adr-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) match the `(narrowing)` arm; `Lint · docs & code guards` and `Check Changeset` are success on the head.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/26724-object-unknown-datasource-refused.md` grades `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch` and carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right: no published type, export or payload widens, and a published accept set narrows (the changeset's own line says the doors refuse a body "which they stored before").

`Metadata-protocol: none` is WRONG for this diff, and so is `patch`. AGENTS.md §3 (line 1088) defines the line as "the change to what a metadata author can write — … a value refused or a requirement tightened is `narrowed`; … `none` all else", and "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves". `datasource` is a key a metadata author writes on `ObjectSchema`; a value an author could write and have stored (`datasource: 'gapdata_nosuch'`, the card's reproduction answered 200 and "published") is now refused, and the requirement that the name resolve is tightened at every door. That is the definition's own example. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (lines 906-931) says the same and says why the gate did not catch it: "a refused value, a narrowed enum or a changed meaning is invisible to [the ratchets], so the declaration — not the diff — is still the carrier"; `Check Changeset` success on this head is therefore not evidence for `none`. The dev's option A ("the refused names never worked; `ObjectSchema.datasource` already declares a datasource ID") argues about the engine's behaviour after the save, not about what the author could write at the door, which is what the line measures. The repo's precedents decide it the same way: #25211, the sibling refusal at these same doors with this same envelope (`.changeset/25211-external-binding-save-doors.md` at `bda53bb0ba`), shipped `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor` with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; #25598 (`escalateTo` refuses a dead target), #25571, #25635, #25650 and #25680 all declare `narrowed` + `minor` for a value refused.

Owed on this head: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` in the changeset body AND on the PR body, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` unchanged (the gate cross-checks `narrowed` against the `(narrowing)` arm, which is present, so the corrected pair passes `check-changeset-no-major`). No other changeset entry is owed: `packages/qa/dogfood` is private and `scripts/` publishes nothing. The dev raised exactly this as `open_questions[0]` and offered to let the seat edit the two lines; the diff on this head carries the wrong value, so this head cannot pass ②.

`Clause-②:` line as read on the PR body and changeset: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (Metadata-protocol none vs narrowed): answered above — B. `narrowed` + `minor`. This is the one change the head owes; it is a changeset and PR-body edit, no code change.
- Dev flag "no path registers a datasource after an HTTP save, so no `needs_decision`": read and confirmed at the head (`ObjectKernel.bootstrap()` completes every phase before the REST doors answer; `driver.*` discovery is in ObjectQL plugin start; `onEnable` registrations are visible to `getDriverByName` by request time). Answered, no escalation.
- Dev flag "an engine without `getDriverByName` cannot say a name is unknown, so nothing is refused on it": matches the spec's optional member; the real engine has it. Answered.
- Dev flag "residue stays re-saveable" / `os migrate meta --stored` does not list such rows: the exemption is as described; a dangling binding on an active row is not repaired by this diff and is not the card's ask. Answered; the datasource DELETE/rename half (`out_of_scope_findings[0]`) is noted and not filed by the dev, and stays out of this review's scope — the seat may file it.
- Dev flag: dogfood battery exit 1 on this head in `packaged-action-disabled-dispatch-live.dogfood.test.ts` (#26572's file; `out_of_scope_findings[1]`): recorded in ① question 6; that file touches nothing this diff changes. Not escalated here; the seat should carry it to #26572's thread.
- Dev flag "merge-tree vs #26708's head `0da44906` auto-merges `protocol.ts`": not re-measured (read-only); the only conflict the dev names is in a file this diff does not touch. Answered.
- Check-runs still in progress at review time: Build Core, Test Core 1/8-8/8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. The dev reports the package suite (21685 passed) and typecheck exit 0 locally, the latter run before the fixture-only head commit. The seat reads these at ACCEPT; a FAIL on ② makes a new head necessary anyway.
